chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Umar ibn Yazid, from Burayd al-Ajli, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who manumitted his slave by contract (mukatabah) for one thousand dirhams, and did not stipulate at the time of contract that if he were unable to pay the full amount, he would return to slavery. The mukatab paid his master five hundred dirhams, then the mukatab died, leaving wealth and a mature son. He said: 'Half of whatever the mukatab left is for the master who contracted with him, and the remaining half is for the son of the mukatab, because he died half free and half slave. When he pays the one who contracted with his father what remained on his father, he is free, with no claim of anyone from the people upon him.'

key_terms.رد في الرق: Return to slavery; a clause where failure to pay results in reverting to full slave status
key_terms.مدرک: Mature/competent (referring to an heir capable of inheriting)
key_terms.مكاتب: A slave who has entered into a contract of manumission
key_terms.مكاتبة: Contract of manumission where a slave pays a lump sum or installments for freedom
key_terms.نصف حر: Half-free; a state where half the manumission price is paid, granting partial freedom

ai.seo_question: What happens to the estate of a slave who dies during his contract of manumission (mukatabah)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the mukatab’s status is simultaneously half-free and half-slave, resulting in an equal division of his estate between the master (to settle the residual debt) and his son (as heir). This ruling underscores the unique legal hybridity of the mukatab, ensuring that upon full payment of the remaining balance by the heir, the slave achieves complete manumission without further obligation to the master.
